intro: You have arrived at Klaros, the Sanctuary of Apollo, in İzmir province. Its story is said to reach back to the 13th century BC. This was the renowned oracular sanctuary of Apollo, belonging to Kolophon — a place whose fame rivalled Delphi and Didyma. Come, let us listen to what the god once had to say.
history: Tradition places the founding of the sanctuary in the 13th century BC. The Doric oracular temple of Apollo was begun in the 3rd century BC and only completed under Hadrian, and the oracle kept speaking until the 4th century AD. A sacred road 2 km long linked the sanctuary to Notion. Then alluvium slowly covered it and kept it buried for centuries — and that is exactly why it survives so exceptionally well preserved today.
structure-2: Pause here at the Altar of Artemis. Apollo was not the only deity honoured at Klaros: this altar was built for the cult of Artemis.
structure-4: Now come closer to the heart of the oracle: the Oracular Crypt, the adyton. In this underground chamber at Klaros, the oracles were delivered. Imagine the hush down here as a question waited for its answer.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Apollo, then the Propylon, and finally the Sacred Way.
facts: Did you know? In the temple cella, fragments of the cult statues of Apollo, Artemis and Leto still lie in place. The seated Apollo is thought to have stood nearly eight metres high, and even the surviving feet and hands show how colossal these figures were. The sanctuary also holds the 'hekatomb' block, used to tether a hundred sacrificial animals. And this was, above all, an oracle of Apollo: in a chamber beneath the temple the prophet drank from the sacred spring and gave the answer in verse. Those vaulted oracular chambers and the water channel beneath the temple survive, and you can still see the stair the prophet went down.
outro: Our journey through Klaros, the Sanctuary of Apollo, ends here. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. The oracle has fallen silent, but these stones still speak to those who listen. Enjoy your visit.
